# PREAMBLE

<br>

## Purpose of this session

<br>


During this training session, we will **integrate** a pair of samples into a single `SeuratObject` and into the same **multidimensional space**.

<br>

## The integration data set

We will still use data from the [Paiva et al.](https://www.cell.com/cell-reports/fulltext/S2211-1247(21)00281-3) publication.
    
While we focused on the **KO sample `TD3a`** until now, we will integrate it with its **wild-type** control counterpart **`TDCT`**.

`TDCT` was pre-processed in a very **similar manner** (QC, doublets, filtering) to what you performed for `TD3A`.

As the purpose is to **integrate** both samples into a single analytical entity, the objects we will use as input are `SeuratObjects` synced up to barcodes **filtering (bad quality, doublets)** (thus, there are no *dimension reduction* data in these objects)

<br>
<br>

# Warm-up !

## Setting global parameters

-   We set the **common parameters** we will use throughout this session :

```{r}
#| label: setparam
#| filename: setparam

## Setting the project name
project_name <- "ebaii_sc_teachers"  # Do not copy-paste this ! It's MY project !!

## Seed for the RNG (our sole parameter for this session)
my_seed <- 1337L

## Some gene markers of cell types of interest
# cell_markers <- c('Il2ra', 'Cd4', 'Cd5', 'Cdc6', 'Lyz2')
cell_markers <- c('Rag1', 'Bcat2', 
                  'Ccnd3', 'Ifngr1', 
                  'Cd5', 'Cd2', 
                  'Il2ra', 'Ptcra', 
                  'Pbk', 'Esco2', 
                  'Ybx3', 
                  'Rtp4', 
                  'Trbv29', 'Trbv13-2', 
                  'C1qa', 
                  'Itgae',
                  'Cd4', 'Cdc6', 'Lyz2')

## Features reduction
hvgs <- 3000

## Variables to regress
vars_to_reg <- c('percent_rb', 'CC_Seurat_SmG2M.Score', 'nCount_RNA')

## PCA
pca_dims <- 50

## Clustering
### Algorithm
clust_algo <- 4  ## Leiden
### Resolution
clust_res <- .6

## Just an environment variable to fix contextual bugs that may happen when our Seurat objects get really big
# options(future.globals.maxSize = 1E+09)
```

# Prepare the data structure

We will do as usual, just editing the session name
:

```{r}
#| label: create_struc
#| filename: create_struc

## PROJECT directory path
project_dir <- paste0("/shared/projects/", project_name)

## Test on PROJECT directory
if (dir.exists(project_dir)) {
  
  ## TD directory path
  TD_dir <- paste0(project_dir, "/SC_TD")
  
  ## SESSION directory path
  session_dir <- paste0(TD_dir, "/06_Integration")
  
  ##INPUT data directory path
  input_dir <- paste0(session_dir, "/DATA")
  
  ## OUTPUT data directory path
  output_dir <- paste0(session_dir, "/RESULTS")
  
  ## Creating the required directores
  dir.create(path = input_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = TRUE)
  dir.create(path = output_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = TRUE)
  
} else {
  warning("Provided project directory [", project_dir, "] does not exist !")
}
```

# Load input data

<br>

The data consists in a **pair of `SeuratObject`s** saved as RDS, one per sample.

<br>

## Fetch data

<br>

We can retrieve the input data :

<br>

```{r}
#| label: backup_integr
#| filename: backup_integr

## Copy the requested files from a local backup, return their user-based local paths

### The TD3A SeuratObject
TD3A_rds <- backup_get_data(
  backup_file = "/shared/projects/2621_eb3in1_2026/atelier_scrnaseq/DATA_BACKUP/INPUT/RDS/TD3A_Filtered_12508.4038.RDS",
  local_path = input_dir,
  force = TRUE)

### The TDCT SeuratObject
TDCT_rds <- backup_get_data(
  backup_file = "/shared/projects/2621_eb3in1_2026/atelier_scrnaseq/DATA_BACKUP/INPUT/RDS/TDCT_Filtered_12254.3671.RDS",
  local_path = input_dir,
  force = TRUE)
```

<br>

## Load into R

<br>

```{r}
#| label: rds_load
#| filename: rds_load

## Loading TD3A
TD3A_so <- readRDS(file = TD3A_rds)

## Loading TDCT
TDCT_so <- readRDS(file = TDCT_rds)

```

# Merge datasets

-   We simply merge the two objects into a single one :

```{r}
#| label: integr_merge
#| filename: integr_merge

TDCT_TD3A_merged <- base::merge(
  x = TDCT_so, # <1>
  y = TD3A_so, # <2>
  add.cell.ids = c("TDCT", "TD3A"), # <3>
  project = paste(c("TDCT", "TD3A"), collapse = "_")) # <4>
```

1.  First object to merge
2.  Second object to merge
3.  Keep track of sample of origin for cells (optional)
4.  Add a new project name (optional but recommended)

<br>

::: {.callout-note}
If you have more than 2 samples to merge, here is the way :

```{r}
#| label: multi_merge
#| filename: multi_merge
#| eval: FALSE

sobj_list <- list(sobj1, sobj2, sobj3, sobj4, sobj5) # <1>

sample_names <- c("S1", "S2", "S3", "S4", "S5") # <2>

MULTIMERGE <- base::merge(
  x = sobj_list[[1]], # <3>
  y = sobj_list[-1], # <4>
  add.cell.ids = sample_names, # <5>
  project = "MULTIMERGE") # <6>
```

1.  A **`list`** of `Seurat` objects (loaded into R)
2.  A **`vector`** of sample names (same length as `sobj_list`)
3.  The **first element** of the `sobj_list`
4.  **All but** the first element of the `sobj_list`
5.  The sample names
6.  The new project name
:::

```{r eval = FALSE, echo=FALSE}
## GOOD
# hvgs <- 3000
# vars_to_reg <- c('percent_rb', 'CC_Seurat_SmG2M.Score', 'nCount_RNA')
# pca_dims_use <- 20
# cluster_res <- .6

## TEST PROCESS
hvgs <- 3000
# vars_to_reg <- c('percent_rb', 'percent_mt', 'CC_Seurat_SmG2M.Score', 'nCount_RNA')
vars_to_reg <- c('percent_rb', 'CC_Seurat_SmG2M.Score', 'nCount_RNA')
pca_dims <- 50
pca_dims_use <- 20
cluster_algo <- 4
cluster_res <- .6

## PROC
TDCT_TD3A_merged <- Seurat::NormalizeData(
  object = TDCT_TD3A_merged, 
  verbose = FALSE)
TDCT_TD3A_merged <- Seurat::FindVariableFeatures(
  object = TDCT_TD3A_merged, 
  nfeatures = hvgs, 
  verbose = FALSE)
TDCT_TD3A_merged <- Seurat::ScaleData(
  object = TDCT_TD3A_merged, 
  vars.to.regress = vars_to_reg, 
  verbose = FALSE)
TDCT_TD3A_merged <- Seurat::RunPCA(
  object = TDCT_TD3A_merged, 
  npcs = pca_dims, 
  verbose = FALSE)

## HARMONY
set.seed(my_seed)
TDCT_TD3A_merged <- harmony:::RunHarmony.Seurat(
  object = TDCT_TD3A_merged,
  reduction.use = 'pca',
  dims.use = 1:pca_dims_use,
  group.by.vars = 'orig.ident',
  reduction.save = "harmony",
  verbose = TRUE)

## CLUSTERING
TDCT_TD3A_merged <- Seurat::FindNeighbors(
  object = TDCT_TD3A_merged, 
  reduction = "harmony", 
  dims = 1:pca_dims_use, 
  graph.name = "snn_harm")
TDCT_TD3A_merged <- Seurat::FindClusters(
  object = TDCT_TD3A_merged,
  graph.name = "snn_harm",
  resolution = cluster_res, 
  algorithm = cluster_algo,
  random.seed = my_seed)
table(TDCT_TD3A_merged$seurat_clusters, TDCT_TD3A_merged$orig.ident)

## CLUSTIFYR ====
# immgen_rds <- "/shared/projects/2621_eb3in1_2026/atelier_scrnaseq/DATA_BACKUP/RESOURCES/ImmGenData.RDS"
# immgen <- readRDS(file = immgen_rds)
### Prep ref
ref_expr <- SummarizedExperiment::assay(immgen, "logcounts")
ref_labels <- as.character(immgen$label.fine)
ref_mat <- clustifyr::average_clusters(mat = ref_expr, metadata = ref_labels, if_log = TRUE)
### Annotate
TDCT_TD3A_merged$immgen_CF_clusters_labels <- clustifyr::clustify(
  input = SeuratObject::JoinLayers(object = TDCT_TD3A_merged, assay = Seurat::DefaultAssay(TDCT_TD3A_merged)),
  ref_mat = ref_mat,
  cluster_col = "seurat_clusters",
  obj_out = TRUE
)$type

## COMPUTE UMAP ====
TDCT_TD3A_merged <- Seurat::RunUMAP(
  object = TDCT_TD3A_merged, 
  reduction = "harmony", 
  dims = 1:pca_dims_use, 
  seed = my_seed,
  reduction.name = "umap_harmony",
  verbose = FALSE)

## Plot UMAP
### SAMPLES
Seurat::DimPlot(
  object = TDCT_TD3A_merged, 
  reduction = "umap_harmony",
  group.by = "orig.ident", 
  shuffle = TRUE,
  seed = my_seed)+
ggplot2::ggtitle("Samples")+
Seurat::DarkTheme()
### CLUSTERS
data("Light24", package = "Polychrome")
cluster_cols <- setNames(
  object = Light24[seq_len(nlevels(TDCT_TD3A_merged$seurat_clusters))],   nm = levels(TDCT_TD3A_merged$seurat_clusters))
# cluster_cols <- setNames(
#   object = Polychrome::palette36.colors(nlevels(TDCT_TD3A_merged$seurat_clusters)),   nm = levels(TDCT_TD3A_merged$seurat_clusters))
Seurat::DimPlot(
  object = TDCT_TD3A_merged, 
  reduction = "umap_harmony",
  group.by = "seurat_clusters", 
  shuffle = TRUE,
  cols = cluster_cols,
  seed = my_seed)+
ggplot2::ggtitle("Clusters")+
Seurat::DarkTheme()
### IMMGEN (clustifyr)
Seurat::DimPlot(
  object = TDCT_TD3A_merged, 
  reduction = "umap_harmony",
  group.by = "immgen_CF_clusters_labels", 
  shuffle = TRUE,
  seed = my_seed)+
ggplot2::ggtitle("Clustifyr")+
Seurat::DarkTheme()

## MARKERS
all_markers <- Seurat::FindAllMarkers(
  object = SeuratObject::JoinLayers(
    object = TDCT_TD3A_merged, 
    assay = Seurat::DefaultAssay(TDCT_TD3A_merged)),
  only.pos = TRUE,
  min.pct = 0.25,
  logfc.threshold = 0.25,
  random.seed = my_seed)
top10_markers <- as.data.frame(all_markers |> dplyr::group_by(cluster) |> dplyr::top_n(n = 10, wt = avg_log2FC))

### HEATMAP
Seurat::DoHeatmap(object = TDCT_TD3A_merged, features = top10_markers$gene) + Seurat::NoLegend()

### DOTPLOT
Seurat::DotPlot(object = TDCT_TD3A_merged, 
                features = unique(top10_markers$gene)) +
  ggplot2::scale_colour_gradient2(low = "red",
                                  mid = "lightgrey",
                                  high = "blue",
                                  midpoint = 0) +
  ## Just aesthetics
  ggplot2::theme(axis.text.x = ggplot2::element_text(angle = 90, 
                                                     vjust = 1,
                                                     size = 8, 
                                                     hjust = 1)) 
```


<br>

::: {.callout-note}
We used the `base::merge()` function, thus the one natively packaged with R, but one can see that we used a parameter specific to `SeuratObject` : `add.cell.ids`, which can sound counterintuitive.

This is because the **base::merge()** function, while being a generic one **can be modified** in the shadows by additional packages, so that it adapts to **objects with new formats**.
:::

<br>

We can get a quick summary of the merged `SeuratObject` :

<br>

```{r}
#| label: merged_smry
#| filename: merged_smry

## A summary of the merged object
TDCT_TD3A_merged
```

<br>

::: {.callout-note icon="false" style="background: lightblue"}
## QUESTION 1A

What can you guess from the dimensions of `TDCT_TD3A_merged` on **the way it was merged** ?
:::

<br>

::: {.callout-note icon="false" collapse="true"}
## A HINT ?

To get to the answer, you'll have to **compare** its dimensions to those of the individual objects.
:::

<br>

::: {.callout-note icon="false" collapse="true" style="background: lightgreen"}
## ANSWER 1A

We check the dimensions of the three objects :

```{r}
#| label: dim_comp
#| filename: dim_comp

knitr::kable(
  data.frame(
    Dataset = c('TD3A', 'TDCT', 'Merged'),
    Nrow= c(nrow(TD3A_so), nrow(TDCT_so), nrow(TDCT_TD3A_merged)),
    Ncol= c(ncol(TD3A_so), ncol(TDCT_so), ncol(TDCT_TD3A_merged))), 
  padding = 0,
  format.args = list(big.mark = ",")) |>
  kableExtra::kable_styling(
    bootstrap_options = "bordered",
    full_width = FALSE)
```

<br>

One can see that the **numbers of cells add up**, but **not those of features** !
:::

<br>
<br>

::: {.callout-note icon="false" style="background: lightblue"}
## QUESTION 1B

Thus, What can you actually guess **what happened for features** ?
:::

<br>

::: {.callout-note icon="false" collapse="true" style="background: lightgreen"}
## ANSWER 1B

We can compare the features in the individual and merged objects :

```{r}
#| label: featnames_comp
#| filename: featnames_comp

### Common features
feats_common <- intersect(
  SeuratObject::Features(TDCT_so), 
  SeuratObject::Features(TD3A_so))
message("Common features : ", length(feats_common))

### TD3A only
TD3A_specific <- setdiff(
  SeuratObject::Features(TD3A_so), 
  SeuratObject::Features(TDCT_so))
message("TD3A-specific : ", length(TD3A_specific))

### TDCT only
TDCT_specific <- setdiff(
  SeuratObject::Features(TDCT_so), 
  SeuratObject::Features(TD3A_so))
message("TDCT-specific : ", length(TDCT_specific))

### TOTAL
message("Sum = ", sum(length(feats_common), 
                      length(TD3A_specific), 
                      length(TDCT_specific)))
```

So, `Seurat` performed the **union** of the features from both individual objects
:::

<br>

::: {.callout-note}
This would remain true for **any number** of individual objects to merge !
:::

<br>

Now a bit of cleaning :

<br>

```{r}
#| label: merge_clean
#| filename: merge_clean

## Clean unneeded objects
rm(TD3A_so, TDCT_so, feats_common, TD3A_specific, TDCT_specific)
```

<br>
<br>

## Process the merged dataset

In order to visualize the data in a 2-D space, one needs to process it the way we learnt :

```{r}
#| label: merge_proc
#| filename: merge_proc
#| attr.output: '.details summary="Show output"'

## Log-normalization
TDCT_TD3A_merged <- Seurat::NormalizeData(
  object = TDCT_TD3A_merged, 
  verbose = FALSE)

## Idenfication of HVGs
TDCT_TD3A_merged <- Seurat::FindVariableFeatures(
  object = TDCT_TD3A_merged, 
  nfeatures = hvgs, 
  verbose = FALSE)

## Scaling
TDCT_TD3A_merged <- Seurat::ScaleData(
  object = TDCT_TD3A_merged, 
  vars.to.regress = vars_to_reg, 
  verbose = FALSE)

## PCA
TDCT_TD3A_merged <- Seurat::RunPCA(
  object = TDCT_TD3A_merged, 
  npcs = pca_dims, 
  verbose = FALSE)
```

We keep a backup of this merged, processed object for later work :

```{r}
#| label: bak
#| filename: bak
#| 
TDCT_TD3A_bak <- TDCT_TD3A_merged
```


```{r}
#| label: merge_elbow
#| filename: merge_elbow
#| fig-align: "center"
#| fig-cap: "Elbow plot (merged)"

Seurat::ElbowPlot(object = TDCT_TD3A_merged, 
                  ndims = pca_dims, 
                  reduction = "pca")
```

We decide to keep the first **`20`** PCs.

```{r}
#| label: dims_kept
#| filename: dims_kept
#| 
dims_kept <- 20
```


## Visualization of the batch effect

### At the covariates level

```{r}
#| label: merge_acov
#| filename: merge_acov
#| fig-width: 11
#| fig-height: 8
#| fig-align: "center"
#| fig-cap: "Covariates weight on PCs (pre-post regression)"

## Assessing un-regressed data (unscaled as proxy)
AC1 <- assess_covar(
  mat = as.matrix(SeuratObject::LayerData(
    object = SeuratObject::JoinLayers(TDCT_TD3A_merged, assay = "RNA"),
    assay = "RNA",
    layer = "data")),
  covar.df = TDCT_TD3A_merged[[]], 
  markers = cell_markers, 
  ndim = 10L, 
  center = TRUE, 
  scale = TRUE, 
  plot = FALSE, 
  title = "Normalized", 
  return.weights = FALSE, 
  return.plot = TRUE)

## Assessing regressed data (scaled)
AC2 <- assess_covar(
  mat = SeuratObject::LayerData(
    object = TDCT_TD3A_merged, 
    assay = "RNA", 
    layer = "scale.data"), 
  covar.df = TDCT_TD3A_merged[[]], 
  markers = cell_markers, 
  ndim = 10L, 
  center = FALSE, 
  scale = FALSE, 
  plot = FALSE, 
  title = "Scaled", 
  return.weights = FALSE, 
  return.plot = TRUE)

## Stack plots
cowplot::plot_grid(grid::grid.grabExpr(ComplexHeatmap::draw(AC1)), grid::grid.grabExpr(ComplexHeatmap::draw(AC2)), ncol = 1, align = "v")
```

# Sample-aware regression

May one use the sample of origin as a covariate to regress ?

::: {.callout-note icon="false" style="background: pink"}
## DEMO

Processing, adding the sample name as a new covariate to regress :

```{r}
#| label: sample_regr_proc
#| filename: sample_regr_proc
#| attr.output: '.details summary="Show output"'

## Log-normalization
TDCT_TD3A_sreg <- Seurat::NormalizeData(
  object = TDCT_TD3A_bak, 
  verbose = FALSE)

## Idenfication of HVGs
TDCT_TD3A_sreg <- Seurat::FindVariableFeatures(
  object = TDCT_TD3A_sreg, 
  nfeatures = hvgs, 
  verbose = FALSE)

## Scaling
TDCT_TD3A_sreg <- Seurat::ScaleData(
  object = TDCT_TD3A_sreg, 
  vars.to.regress = unique(c('orig.ident', vars_to_reg)),       # <1>
  verbose = FALSE)

## PCA
TDCT_TD3A_sreg <- Seurat::RunPCA(
  object = TDCT_TD3A_sreg, 
  npcs = pca_dims, 
  verbose = FALSE)
```

1.  Here we add the sample name (`orig.ident`) as a new covariate to regress

<br>

Elbow plot :

```{r}
#| label: sample_regr_elbow
#| filename: sample_regr_elbow
#| fig-align: "center"
#| fig-cap: "Elbow plot (sample-regressed)"

Seurat::ElbowPlot(object = TDCT_TD3A_sreg, 
                  ndims = pca_dims, 
                  reduction = "pca")
```

Assessing the remaining weight of covariates :

```{r}
#| label: sample_regr_acov
#| filename: sample_regr_acov
#| fig-width: 11
#| fig-height: 8
#| fig-align: "center"
#| fig-cap: "Covariates weight on PCs (w, w/o sample regression)"

## Assessing un-regressed data (unscaled as proxy)

## Assessing the covariates weight after regression
AC3 <- assess_covar(
  mat = SeuratObject::LayerData(
    object = TDCT_TD3A_sreg, 
    assay = "RNA", 
    layer = "scale.data"), 
  covar.df = TDCT_TD3A_sreg[[]], 
  markers = cell_markers, 
  ndim = 10L, 
  center = FALSE, 
  scale = FALSE, 
  plot = FALSE, 
  title = "Scaled, sample-regressed", 
  return.weights = FALSE, 
  return.plot = TRUE)

## Comparison to the simple merge
cowplot::plot_grid(grid::grid.grabExpr(ComplexHeatmap::draw(AC2)), grid::grid.grabExpr(ComplexHeatmap::draw(AC3)), ncol = 1, align = "v")
```

# Integration

We will perform integration using multiple methods.

## Multiple methods
:::{.panel-tabset}

### Seurat : CCA

We will use the [CCA](https://satijalab.org/seurat/reference/ccaintegration) method.

Integration

```{r}
#| label: integr_s_cca
#| filename: integr_s_cca
#| attr.output: '.details summary="Show output"'

TDCT_TD3A_merged <- Seurat::IntegrateLayers(
  object = TDCT_TD3A_merged, 
  orig.reduction = "pca",
  assay = "RNA",
  method = "CCAIntegration", 
  new.reduction = "seurat.cca", 
  normalization.method = "LogNormalize",
  preserve.order = TRUE,
  dims = 1:dims_kept,
  verbose = FALSE)
```

Clustering

```{r}
#| label: s_cca_clust
#| filename: s_cca_clust
#| attr.output: '.details summary="Show output"'

TDCT_TD3A_merged <- Seurat::FindNeighbors(
  object = TDCT_TD3A_merged,
  reduction = "seurat.cca", 
  dims = 1:dims_kept, 
  graph.name = "snn_s.cca",
  verbose = FALSE)

TDCT_TD3A_merged <- Seurat::FindClusters(
  object = TDCT_TD3A_merged,
  graph.name = "snn_s.cca",
  resolution = clust_res, 
  random.seed = my_seed,
  algorithm = clust_algo,
  verbose = FALSE)
```

UMAP

```{r}
#| label: s_cca_umap
#| filename: s_cca_umap
#| attr.output: '.details summary="Show output"'

TDCT_TD3A_merged <- Seurat::RunUMAP(
  object = TDCT_TD3A_merged, 
  reduction = "seurat.cca", 
  dims = 1:dims_kept, 
  seed = my_seed,
  reduction.name = "umap_s.cca",
  verbose = FALSE)
```

```{r}
#| label: s_cca_umap_dp
#| filename: s_cca_umap_dp
#| fig-width: 12
#| fig-height: 6
#| fig-align: "center"
#| fig-cap: "Samples and clusters in UMAP space (Seurat CCA)"

## Visualization at the samples level
S.CCA_samp_dp <- Seurat::DimPlot(object = TDCT_TD3A_merged, 
                                 group.by = "orig.ident", 
                                 reduction = "umap_s.cca", 
                                 shuffle = TRUE,
                                 label.color = "white",
                                 label = TRUE)+ 
  ggplot2::ggtitle("Samples (Seurat CCA)")+
  Seurat::DarkTheme()

## We generate a custom flashy color palette based on the Polychrome:Light24 palette
data("Light24", package = "Polychrome")

cluster_cols <- setNames(
  object = Light24[seq_len(nlevels(TDCT_TD3A_merged[[paste0("snn_s.cca_res.", clust_res), drop = TRUE]]))], 
  nm = levels(TDCT_TD3A_merged[[paste0("snn_s.cca_res.", clust_res), drop = TRUE]]))

## Visualization at the clusters level
S.CCA_dp <- Seurat::DimPlot(object = TDCT_TD3A_merged, 
                            group.by = paste0("snn_s.cca_res.", clust_res), 
                            reduction = "umap_s.cca",
                            shuffle = TRUE,
                            cols = cluster_cols,
                            label.color = "white",
                            label = TRUE)+ 
  ggplot2::ggtitle("Clusters (Seurat CCA)")+
  Seurat::DarkTheme()

S.CCA_samp_dp + S.CCA_dp + patchwork::plot_layout(ncol = 2)
```

### Harmony (PCA embeddings)

Harmony can also be run on PCA embeddings directly.

This is useful when not working with a `SeuratObject`.

::: {.callout-important icon="false" style="background: pink"}
## DEMO

Integration

```{r}
#| label: integr_harmony_pca
#| filename: integr_harmony_pca
#| attr.output: '.details summary="Show output"'

## Fixing the seed
set.seed(my_seed)

## Running Harmony on the PCA reduction, limited to the selected first PCs
HS1 <- harmony:::RunHarmony.default(
  data_mat = SeuratObject::Embeddings(
    object = TDCT_TD3A_merged, 
    reduction = "pca")[,1:dims_kept], 
  meta_data = TDCT_TD3A_merged[[]],
  vars_use = "orig.ident",
  verbose = FALSE)

## Injecting the newly created harmony embedding into the SeuratObject
TDCT_TD3A_merged[["harmony_pca"]] <- Seurat::CreateDimReducObject(
  embeddings = HS1, 
  key = "harmonyS1_", 
  assay = Seurat::DefaultAssay(TDCT_TD3A_merged))

## Cleaning
rm(HS1)
```

Clustering

```{r}
#| label: harmony_pca_clust
#| filename: harmony_pca_clust
#| attr.output: '.details summary="Show output"'

TDCT_TD3A_merged <- Seurat::FindNeighbors(
  object = TDCT_TD3A_merged,
  reduction = "harmony_pca", 
  dims = 1:dims_kept, 
  graph.name = "snn_harmonypca",
  verbose = FALSE)

TDCT_TD3A_merged <- Seurat::FindClusters(
  object = TDCT_TD3A_merged,
  graph.name = "snn_harmonypca",
  resolution = clust_res, 
  random.seed = my_seed,
  algorithm = clust_algo,
  verbose = FALSE)
```

::: {.callout-note}

**Why are there differences between Harmony called by Seurat and standalone ?**

This is a question of **different default parameters**

:::: {.columns .with-divider}

::: {.column width="50%"}
Here is an excerpt of the help for the `Seurat::HarmonyIntegration` wrapper function to Harmony :

```
Seurat::HarmonyIntegration(
  object,
  orig,
  features = NULL,
  scale.layer = "scale.data",
  new.reduction = "harmony",
  layers = NULL,
  npcs = NULL,
  key = "harmony_",
  theta = NULL,                 ## SAME
  lambda = NULL,                ## SAME
  sigma = 0.1,                  ## SAME
  nclust = NULL,                ## SAME
  tau = 0,                      ## SAME
  block.size = 0.05,            ## SAME
  max.iter.harmony = 10L,       ## SAME
  max.iter.cluster = 20L,       ## ! DIFF !
  epsilon.cluster = 1e-05,      ## ! DIFF !
  epsilon.harmony = 0.01,       ## SAME
  verbose = TRUE,
  ...
)
```
:::

::: {.column width="50%"}
And here is the same for Harmony standalone

```
harmony::RunHarmony(
  data_mat,
  meta_data,
  vars_use,
  theta = NULL,                   ## SAME
  sigma = 0.1,                    ## SAME
  lambda = NULL,                  ## SAME
  nclust = NULL,                  ## SAME
  max_iter = 10,                  ## SAME
  early_stop = TRUE,
  ncores = 1,
  plot_convergence = FALSE,
  return_object = FALSE,
  verbose = TRUE,
  .options = harmony_options(),
  ...
)
```

Some parameters are missing here : they are available as **global options**, accessed with `harmony::harmony_options()` :

```
> harmony::harmony_options()
$alpha
[1] 0.2             ## !!! UNK !!!
$tau
[1] 0               ## SAME
$block.size
[1] 0.05            ## SAME
$max.iter.cluster
[1] 4               ## ! DIFF !
$epsilon.cluster
[1] 0.001           ## ! DIFF !
$epsilon.harmony
[1] 0.01            ## SAME
$batch.prop.cutoff
[1] 1e-05           ## !!! UNK !!!
```
:::

:::

This is most probably to **maintain compatibility** of the wrapper with the 1st generation of the `Harmony` method (v1.x).

:::
